successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: south-eastern Sicily and the east coast to Tauromenium

ledger.x: 733 BC: Syracuse 'founded by the Corinthians in 733 BC (according to the Thucydidean dating)'.

485 BC: 'In 485 BC, the aristocracy of Syracuse called the Gamori' sought Gelon's aid and he took the city 'with little or no resistance' (tyrant 485-478); his lands, Gela and, by the page's 491 account, Camarina, join the city: 'forced half the citizens of Gela to move to Syracuse'.
483 BC: Gelon conquers Euboea and Megara Hyblaea; their land joins Syracuse.
405 BC: Dionysius I 'seized total power and became tyrant' (tyrant 405-367).
397 BC: Dionysius I 'fought a war with Carthage from 397 BC to 392 BC with mixed success'.
392 BC: the war with Carthage ends; at Dionysius' death in 367 the Carthaginians 'were still masters of at least a third' of Sicily.
387-385 BC: the Adriatic.
386 BC: 'he took Rhegium in 386 and sold the inhabitants as slaves'; the 387 expedition 'devastated the territories of Thurii and Croton'.

367 BC: Dionysius I dies; the pages say nothing of the Italian and Adriatic holdings under Dionysius II, Dion and Timoleon ('his rule lasted about a decade'), so Rhegium and the colonies are dropped at his death rather than carried blindly.
367 BC: Dionysius II succeeds: 'When his father died in 367 BC'.

357 BC: Dion returns and Dionysius II loses Syracuse; 'Other Sicilian cities broke away and were ruled by local tyrants', so the Sicilian holdings beyond the core (Messina, the interior) leave Syracuse; the page infobox has 356 for the end of the tyranny.
317 BC: 'In 317 BC, Agathocles used this force to launch a coup' (tyrant 317-289).

c. 313 BC: after the peace of 314/313 Agathocles 'quickly brought many cities and fortresses under his control' and took Messina in 313/312 'without a fight'; the cities opposed to him were Acragas, Gela and Messina. The region is my reading.
311-306 BC: Agathocles' war with Carthage 'between 311 and 306 BC', with the 'expedition to Africa'.
311 BC: 'In 311 BC Agathocles was defeated in the Battle of the Himera River and besieged in Syracuse'; he lands in Africa in August 310.
306 BC: 'A peace treaty with Carthage left him in control of Sicily east of the Halycus River.'
306 BC: Sicily east of the Halycus confirmed to Syracuse; Tauromenium 'also fell into his hands'.
304 BC: Agathocles 'styled himself king of Sicily in 304 BC'.
289 BC: Agathocles dies; the Agathocles page 'gives no account of what happened to Syracuse's territory after 289 BC'.
278 BC: 'Late 278: Pyrrhus entered Syracuse after the Carthaginians abandoned their siege'; Syracuse a belligerent on his side 'from 278'.
276 BC: Pyrrhus leaves Sicily.
275 BC: Hiero II.

c. 270-264 BC: the Mamertine war. Hiero 'defeated the Mamertines in a pitched battle near Mylae along the Longanus river'; he besieged Messana in 265 until a Carthaginian fleet 'occupied the harbour of Messina'.
264 BC: Hiero 'joined the Carthaginian leader Hanno', the fighting with Appius Claudius Caudex 'was inconclusive, and Hiero withdrew to Syracuse'.
263 BC: the Roman treaty.

263 BC: 'in 263 he concluded a treaty with Rome, by which he was to rule over the south-east of Sicily and the eastern coast as far as Tauromenium'; 'Until his death he remained loyal to the Romans' (vassal_start syracuse 263 in roman-republic).
215 BC: 'Hieronymus came to the throne in 215 BC after his grandfather's death, and Syracuse fell under an anti-Roman faction'.

215 BC: Hiero II dies and 'Hieronymus came to the throne in 215 BC after his grandfather's death, and Syracuse fell under an anti-Roman faction'; the Hiero II page gives both 215 and 'shortly after the Battle of Cannae in 216'.

214-212 BC: 'War broke out in 214 BC'; Epicydes and Hippocrates 'had retaken the city and named themselves tyrants'; Marcellus 'laid siege to the port city by sea and land in 213 BC' ('Spring 213 - Autumn 212 BC').
212 BC (autumn): the fall.
212 BC: the siege ends.
212 BC: 'Roman siege in 212 BC'; the city capitulated 'under the consul Marcus Claudius Marcellus' and 'was designated the capital of Roman Sicily'.

wars.name: Wars of Dionysius I with Carthage
Agathocles' war with Carthage
wars.outcome: peace of 306: Syracuse keeps 'Sicily east of the Halycus River'

wars.name: Pyrrhic War (Sicilian campaign)
wars.outcome: Pyrrhus takes central Sicily (277), fails at Lilybaeum, leaves (276)

wars.name: Siege of Syracuse
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; the city 'completely sacked'; Sicily one province by 210

certainty.note: A single city's chora with Gelon's additions; the circles are the researcher's.
The Halycus line of 306 and the Tauromenium limit of 263 are the named frontiers; the interior is drawn by modern provinces.
